name: two_factor_shock_with_cross_term_loss
question_template: Use exact arithmetic. A portfolio worth V={V} USD faces two factors: an equity index and an FX rate. Signed equity change is e={E} percent; signed FX change is f={F} percent. Raw equity sensitivity is b={B}; a hedge covers h={H} percent of the equity exposure, so net equity sensitivity is b*(1-h/100). FX sensitivity is d={D}. Interaction coefficient is k={K}: the cross effect on the value ratio is k times the product of the factor ratios e/100 and f/100 (the hedge does not apply to it). Total value ratio is the net equity effect plus the FX effect plus the cross effect; signed value change is V times that ratio. Report the loss magnitude in USD: the positive size of the decline if value falls, otherwise 0.

slots.description: Exact equity sensitivity after the hedge is applied.
Exact signed cross-effect contribution to the value ratio.
Exact signed USD change in portfolio value before taking the loss magnitude.

program:
def solve():
    V = Fraction(P["V"])
    e = Fraction(P["E"]) / 100
    f = Fraction(P["F"]) / 100
    b = Fraction(P["B"])
    d = Fraction(P["D"])
    k = Fraction(P["K"])
    h = Fraction(P["H"]) / 100
    net_b = b * (1 - h)
    equity_effect = net_b * e
    fx_effect = d * f
    cross = k * e * f
    total_ratio = equity_effect + fx_effect + cross
    change = V * total_ratio
    loss = -change if change < 0 else Fraction(0)
    return {
        "final": loss,
        "net_equity_sensitivity": net_b,
        "cross_effect_ratio": cross,
        "signed_value_change": change
    }
